summary: Configured persistent TCP forwarding of `inventory` syslog messages from node2 to node1. Messages are stored at `/var/log/inventory/node2.log`. Verified live delivery and successful recovery after sequential restarts of both nodes.
actions_performed: Configured node1 rsyslog TCP collector on port 514 with an inventory-specific rule.
Added a persistent firewall rule allowing TCP/514 only from node2.
Configured node2 with durable queued TCP forwarding for the `inventory` program name.
Validated both rsyslog configurations and verified end-to-end delivery.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually, proving changed boot identities and post-restart log delivery.

evidence.summary: node1 configuration validated; rsyslog is enabled and listening on TCP/514 with a persistent source-restricted firewall rule.
node2 forwarding configuration validated and rsyslog is active and enabled.
A generated inventory message traversed the TCP connection and appeared at the required path on node1.

Healthy baseline captured; reboot acknowledged; boot ID changed from 325732f1-bc39-4512-b05e-397f42060246 to a88ab6a6-0317-4040-ab05-4ff433dc9458; listener, firewall, retained data, and new message delivery recovered.

Healthy baseline captured; reboot acknowledged; boot ID changed from fe422859-bfe7-4eb4-819b-e09864f3ca60 to 0f6c4df0-d684-4ff7-8d66-4d706a03b1bd; rsyslog recovered, reconnected, and delivered a fresh inventory message to node1.
